chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Salama ibn Muhraz, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'An Armenian man died and bequeathed to me.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'And what is an Armenian?' I said, 'A Nabatean from the Nabateans of the mountains, died and bequeathed to me his legacy, and left a daughter.' So he (peace be upon him) said to me, 'Give her half.'

He (the narrator) said, 'So I informed Zurara of that, and he said to me, 'I was being cautious for you; rather, the wealth is for her.' So I entered upon him (peace be upon him) afterwards and said, 'May Allah improve you! Our companions claimed that you were cautious with me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'No, by Allah, I was not cautious with you, but I was cautious over you lest you be held responsible (for giving too little). So did anyone know of that?' I said, 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So give her what remains.'

key_terms.أَرْمَانِيّاً: Armenian (a specific ethnic group mentioned in the context of non-Arab Muslims)
key_terms.نَبَطِيٌّ: Nabatean (a people from the mountains, used here to clarify the ethnicity)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a daughter who is the sole heir?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'taqiyya' (precautionary dissimulation) in inheritance rulings, where the Imam initially advised giving half to the daughter to protect the executor from potential liability regarding unknown heirs. Upon clarification that no other claimants existed, the Imam corrected the ruling to the full estate, highlighting the distinction between precautionary measures and definitive legal entitlements. This incident underscores the dynamic nature of fiqh where practical wisdom and risk management inform the application of Quranic shares.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Salama Bin Muhraz who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘An Armenian man died and bequeathed to me (to be an executor)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘And what is Armenian?’ I said, ‘Nabatean, from the Nabatean people of the mountain, died, and bequeathed to me with his legacy, and left a daughter’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Give her the half’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I informed Zurara of that, so he said to me, ‘(Out of) dissimulation for you. But rather, the wealth is for her’. So I came up to him<sup>asws</sup> afterwards, so I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you well! Our companions are claiming that you<sup>asws</sup> were dissimulative to me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I<sup>asws</sup> was not dissimulative to you, but I<sup>asws</sup> was protective over you if you were held responsible. So does anyone have the knowledge of that?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So give her what remains’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Salmah ibn Muhriz who has narrated the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that an Armani man has died and has made a will to me. He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is Armaniy?’ I replied, ‘He is a Nabatiy from Nabatiy people of mountains who has died. He has made a will to me about his legacy and has left behind his daughter.’ He (the Imam) said to me, ‘Give her one-half.’

I then informed Zurarah about it and he said, ‘He (the Imam) has been protective ( taqiyah ) of you, otherwise, all the legacy belongs to the daughter.’ He (the narrator) has said that I then visited him (the Imam) afterwards and said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, our people think that you have been protective with me.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, by Allah I have not been protective of you, but I have been protective against you to be held responsible; has anyone had any knowledge of it?’ I replied, ‘No, no one knows.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Give her the rest of her legacy.’”
